description: Grade 5 example: write an interval under a key signature (F major, treble clef).

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 10 addendum)

item.prompt: The key signature of F major is shown. Write the note a perfect 5th down from this note, adding an accidental only if the key signature does not already give it.

music.textAlternative: One minim, F5, under the key signature of F major.

hints: Find the letter name first, then decide what the interval needs on that letter.
Then compare with the key signature: write a sign only for the difference.

feedback.correct: Correct. F down a perfect 5th is B♭. F major's signature already has B♭, so the note is written with no accidental.

mistakes.redundant-or-missing-accidental: F down a perfect 5th is B♭. F major's signature already has B♭, so the note is written with no accidental.
mistakes.accidental-not-applied: Check what the key signature already gives that letter before adding a sign. F down a perfect 5th is B♭. F major's signature already has B♭, so the note is written with no accidental.
mistakes.enharmonic-spelling: That sounds the same but uses the wrong letter name. An interval's number fixes the letter: count the letter names from the starting note.

feedback.fallback: F down a perfect 5th is B♭. F major's signature already has B♭, so the note is written with no accidental.
